reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: Section 19.1 gives the professional-and-workmanlike services warranty plus material conformity; 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable conformity period measured from the later of delivery or acceptance (better than the preferred delivery-only benchmark) and Hosted Services conformity for the whole subscription term (exceeding the 12-month software benchmark); 19.3 covers no malicious code and Applicable Law compliance; 19.4 supplies re-performance/repair/replacement with a termination-and-refund backstop and is expressly non-exclusive; 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties and expressly preserves express warranties, so the disclaimer does not swallow them.
No redline or counterparty comment is expected or provided for a compliant finding, so the empty edit set is correct and the smallest-edit test is satisfied trivially.

The failed deterministic check ('warranty period ≥ 90 days or expressed in months/years') is a false negative caused by the period being spelled out as 'ninety days' rather than '90 days' — the substantive period meets the playbook threshold.

Minor, non-disqualifying observation for internal evidence: the malicious-code warranty is limited to code 'intentionally introduced by Vendor', which is slightly narrower than the preferred 'no malicious code'; this is a common market formulation and does not change the compliant characterization, but the rationale could have flagged it.
